reader.requirement: At --std 85, in both SEARCH formats, a WHEN phrase whose body is NEXT SENTENCE must be refused when END-SEARCH is written, and accepted (transferring to the next sentence) when it is not.

edition-consulted.switches: construct next-sentence-archaic-2023: the archaic flag on NEXT SENTENCE at 2023; not raised at 1985, and not the END-SEARCH screen

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion in StatementValidation.CheckSearchEndSearchNextSentence, SearchBinder.Phrases and StatementBinder.IsNextSentenceArm: none; the screen is the same code at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness runs SEARCH with NEXT SENTENCE; the END-SEARCH refusal in both formats is exercised only by the probes here

probes.printed: COBOL2409 for SEARCH (line 10) and SEARCH ALL (line 14): END-SEARCH specified and a WHEN phrase's body is NEXT SENTENCE
EXIT 0; B NOT-SKIPPED AFTER1 C AFTER2 AFTER3 AFTER4 (NEXT SENTENCE without END-SEARCH in both formats, END-SEARCH with imperative bodies)

reader.notes: One screen serves both formats from Phrases, keyed on the WHEN arm being exactly NEXT SENTENCE. 1985 takes the same arm as 2023.
reader.at-2023: s5 refused the same way at --std 2023 (2 errors)

refuter.evidence: src/s5x.cob (s5x-001): with END-SEARCH, AT END NEXT SENTENCE, a WHEN body 'DISPLAY NEXT SENTENCE', and an IF ... END-IF followed by NEXT SENTENCE in SEARCH ALL are each refused (COBOL2269: NEXT SENTENCE outside the three formats that print it), and a second WHEN whose body is NEXT SENTENCE draws COBOL2409. src/s5y.cob: the same misplacements without END-SEARCH are refused too (COBOL2269), so 1985's phrase-only NEXT SENTENCE is not admitted as a statement. src/s5z.cob (s5z-001, EXIT 0): a SEARCH with a NEXT SENTENCE WHEN body, ended by END-IF or by ELSE of an enclosing IF (GR1c), is accepted and transfers past the period: printed AFTER1 AFTER2 only. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.22.3 SR5  (║6.22.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR5'.
